real_estate.homebuilder: Lennar is paying buyers about 12% to close, and your buyers read the same headlines.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage rates start the week where Friday left them. Mortgage News Daily had the 30-year at 7.20% and the 15-year at 6.83% as of September 18, with Monday's reading due this afternoon. The 10-Year is lending a hand this morning, trading just under 5% after Friday's 5.01% close.

One of the country's biggest builders is doing its discounting out loud. Lennar said last week that its average home sold for $372,000 after about 12.0% in incentives, that new orders fell 9% from a year ago, and that it is trimming its full year delivery target to roughly 80,000 to 81,000 homes, from 82,000 to 83,000. The stock fell 4.10% Friday and is down about 26% this year, a bit worse than the 24% Market Briefs printed.

Lennar's average home sells for less than a third of Fremont's median, so this is not head to head competition. But your buyers read the same headlines, and when a national builder is paying 12% to get deals closed, the buyer at your open house walks in expecting somebody to blink.

• The local math: at Fremont's median list price of $1,200,000, 10% down means a $1,080,000 loan, still under Alameda County's $1,249,125 high-balance conforming limit.
• At 7.20%, principal and interest alone run about $7,331 a month, and every eighth of a point is about $92.
• Keeping that to 30% of gross pay takes about $293,000 a year, and that is before property tax, insurance and mortgage insurance.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Board wide: 2,763 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 193 coming soon and 223 brand new.
• Five city ledger: 717 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 632 are already on the market and 85 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 254 live, 200 active, 37 coming soon, 17 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,200,000 at $794 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 31 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 188, Milpitas 114, Newark 92, Union City 69.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,098,444 at $680 a square foot. 286 homes are priced under a million, and 167 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

What this means for you: the ledger held at 717, but homes sitting 60 days or longer rose to 167 from 161, the slow drain we charted yesterday showing up in the daily count. Buyers: when the biggest builders are paying 12% to close, asking a seller to help with a rate buydown is a normal request, not an insult. Sellers: past 30 days in Fremont, the conversation is price, not patience.

economy.note: All four are Friday, September 18. The 10-Year is the Treasury daily yield curve close, gold and silver are the COMEX front month at Friday's 1:00 PM PT print measured against Thursday's same time print, and Brent is the ICE front month (November contract) settlement.
economy.commentary:
Japan raised its benchmark rate to 1.25% on Friday, the highest since 1995. It is the Bank of Japan's sixth increase since March 2024, counting the move out of negative rates, and it came three months after the last one. The vote was 7 to 2, and the change takes effect September 24, after three Japanese holidays.

Why should a Fremont buyer care? Japan owns more U.S. Treasuries than any other country, $1.10 trillion as of July by the Treasury's own count, and it has trimmed about $82 billion of them since the end of 2025. When Japanese bonds pay more at home, some of that money stays home, and fewer buyers for Treasuries tends to mean higher yields. Your mortgage rate follows the 10-Year, not the Fed.

A correction on oil. Sunday's edition said Brent fell 5.28% on Friday to $99.29. That number belonged to the December contract. The front month contract, the one we report, settled Friday at $103.87, down 0.91%, exactly as Saturday's edition had it. Our price feed briefly swapped contracts over the weekend and we should have caught it. This morning the drop is real: Brent is trading near $100, down about 3.7% for a fourth straight losing session.

Gold and silver both gave back just under 1% this morning after Friday's gains, gold near $4,387 and silver near $66.64.

feature_images.alt: Step chart of the Bank of Japan policy rate target from January 2024 to September 2026. It moves from minus 0.1% to a 0 to 0.1% range in March 2024, then 0.25% in July 2024, 0.5% in January 2025, 0.75% in December 2025, 1.0% in June 2026 and 1.25% on September 18, 2026, the highest since 1995.
feature_images.caption: Japan's policy rate has gone from below zero to 1.25% in two and a half years, six increases in all. The last time its overnight rate averaged this much was June 1995.
